chapters.title: Sign in and home
chapters.intro: Everyone starts at the sign-in page and lands on Home. Home looks different for a researcher, who hands out work, and for a reviewer, who does it. This chapter also shows what a stranger sees and what happens with a broken link.

steps.title: The sign-in page
steps.click: Look at the page. It has the email and password fields, Sign in, Sign in with a passkey, Sign in with your organisation, Email me a code, Forgot your password? and Create an account.
steps.expect: The page loads with every sign-in option. Nothing else of the app is visible.
steps.why: This is the only door into the app. Every other step starts behind it.

steps.title: A signed-out visitor is sent to sign in
steps.click: In the private window, open the link.
steps.expect: You do not see My work. The app sends you to the sign-in page, and after you sign in it brings you back to My work.
steps.why: Nothing in the app may show to someone who has not signed in, and a deep link must still work after signing in.

steps.title: Create an account
steps.click: Look at the form with Create account. Do not send it, because it would make a real account. The second step asks for the emailed code with Confirm and set up, Resend the code and Change it.
steps.expect: The form loads. A link Sign in leads back to the sign-in page.
steps.why: A new pathologist or researcher can join without an invitation, and then sets up a workspace.

steps.title: An invitation link that does not work
steps.click: Open the link. It moves on to /invite by itself.
steps.expect: The page says This invite link does not work. No account form shows.
steps.why: Old or withdrawn invitations must fail clearly instead of half working.

steps.title: The invite landing
steps.click: With a real invitation this page shows the workspace and the inviter, Accept and create my account, Join and open my first slide, Decline, I already have an account, sign in, and a box I agree to the terms and the data processing agreement. With this made-up token it shows the error.
steps.expect: This invite link does not work.
steps.why: This is how a reviewer joins a project they were invited to, and the terms must be agreed before the account exists.

steps.title: Sign in as the researcher and land on Home
steps.click: Sign in at /sign-in with role-researcher@parfocal.eu. In the top bar open the workspace switcher, Switch workspace, and pick ČVUT · Biomedical Engineering.
steps.expect: Home shows the three projects with their slide counts, the week's numbers with open disagreements, a getting started checklist and buttons New project, New review task and Run a model.
steps.why: Home is where a researcher sees what needs them today, such as open disagreements and slides without results.

steps.title: The top bar and the sidebar
steps.click: Look at the top bar: the Parfocal logo, Switch workspace, the search box, New project, Upload, the jobs button, the bell and your avatar. Then the sidebar: Home, My work, Search, the projects with their slide counts, Team. Press Hide the sidebar and Show the sidebar.
steps.expect: Every item opens its page. Admin is missing, because the researcher has no admin rights.
steps.why: These are the ways around the whole app. Knowing them makes every later step quicker.

steps.title: Home for a reviewer
steps.click: Press Log out in the avatar menu and sign in as role-reviewer-a@parfocal.eu, or use a second private window. Look at Continue where you left off.
steps.expect: Home leads with one big Continue where you left off button for Role account review, then the tasks due.
steps.why: A reviewer should get from sign-in to the next object in one click.

steps.title: The first-run setup
steps.click: Walk through the five steps You, Workspace, First project, Viewer and Done with Next and Back. Pick Researcher or Reviewer, a device such as Mouse or Trackpad and a theme Dark, Light or System. Use Skip this step instead of creating a workspace.
steps.expect: Each step shows its choices. Nothing is created unless you press Create my first project or Create a new workspace.
steps.why: A new user picks their role and input device once, and the viewer then fits how they work.

steps.title: The old projects address goes home
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: You land on Home, which lists the projects. There is no separate projects list page.
steps.why: Old bookmarks still lead somewhere useful.

steps.title: A page that does not exist
steps.click: Open the link, then press Go home.
steps.expect: Page not found. This page does not exist, or it was moved or deleted. Go home brings you back.
steps.why: A mistyped or stale link must never show a blank screen.

chapters.title: Projects and upload
chapters.intro: A project holds slides, AI results, cases and tasks. Each workspace has three seeded projects: the study project Sentinel node metastasis study, the gallery project Scanner format comparison with one slide of every supported format, and the clinical project Breast surgery sentinel nodes with cases and reports.

steps.title: Start a new project
steps.click: The New project drawer opens over Home. Look at Name, Privacy, Class list and Analysis template. Press Cancel, or Create and upload if you want a throwaway project, which a reseed removes.
steps.expect: The drawer shows every field. Create and upload makes the project and opens its upload page.
steps.why: The privacy mode and class list are chosen here and decide what reviewers may see and which classes they can pick.

steps.title: The project page and its Slides tab
steps.click: Look at the header buttons Upload, New case and New review task, and the More menu with Run a model, Automatic imports and Project settings. On the Slides tab, type in Filter by slide, file or case.
steps.expect: Slides list with their state, such as Case ready, Case in-review, Case signed-off and Case ai-running, each with its results.
steps.why: This is the researcher's home for one study, where every slide and its progress shows at a glance.

steps.title: The Review tasks tab
steps.click: Open the Review tasks tab. Each row has the task code such as RT-10, its name, progress and buttons Disagreements and Evaluation.
steps.expect: Every seeded task shows, from Every state review to Class decision queue example, with the annotate task Tumour annotation marked as annotate.
steps.why: From here a researcher reaches the queue, the sign-off and the report of every task.

steps.title: The Settings tab
steps.click: Open Settings. Look at Invite people, the class list with Add a class, the opinion form with Edit the form, the members with Manage, and Delete project at the bottom. Do not delete.
steps.expect: Everything is editable, because the researcher owns the project.
steps.why: The class list, the opinion form and who is in the project are set here once and used by every task.

steps.title: A viewer cannot change the project settings
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: The settings show read only with the line Only an owner of this project changes its settings.
steps.why: A viewer such as a student or an auditor may look at everything and change nothing.

steps.title: Upload, the Files step
steps.click: The page has three steps, Files, Check and Upload. Pick From this computer or From a link or storage, then Choose files or a folder. Open What files work? to see the folder shape Parfocal understands.
steps.expect: With nothing picked the page says Add at least one slide to go on. Results go with a slide. Picked files show as one list grouped by case and slide.
steps.why: Slides and AI results arrive together, and the app pairs each result with its slide before anything is uploaded.

steps.title: Upload, the Check and Upload steps
steps.click: With a slide picked, press Next. Under Pair results by choose Folder, then name, then ID, and under Cases choose From folder names or Keep all loose. Each problem has its fix, such as Leave it out, and a slide already in the project offers Skip it or Keep both. Press Next to start, then Open now with what is ready or Run a model.
steps.expect: One bar per file and one for everything. You can leave the page and the upload keeps going in the jobs tray.
steps.why: Big slide files take minutes, so the upload must survive leaving the page and must show every problem before it starts.

steps.title: The format gallery
steps.click: Look at the slide list.
steps.expect: 15 slides, one per format: Aperio SVS with JPEG and JPEG 2000, Hamamatsu NDPI, Leica SCN, Ventana BIF, Philips TIFF, Huron, Argos AVS, generic TIFF, MIRAX, DICOM, OME-TIFF, and the sample test_065.
steps.why: Every format a scanner writes must open natively. This project is the proof.

steps.title: Compare two slides from the list
steps.click: Tick two slides, such as CMU-1.tiff and CMU-1.ndpi, and press Compare. Edit slides lets you rename or move them.
steps.expect: The viewer opens both side by side, and moving one moves the other.
steps.why: A researcher checks the same tissue from two scanners in one view.

steps.title: Make a new case
steps.click: The New case drawer opens over the clinical project. Look at Case ID, Patient and Specimen. Press Cancel, or Create case for a throwaway case.
steps.expect: The drawer fits the window. Create case adds the case and offers to upload its slides.
steps.why: In a clinical project, slides belong to a patient's case, which ends in a signed clinical report.

steps.title: Upload slides into a case
steps.click: The case upload drawer has Upload slides, Drop slides here and Choose file. During an upload it shows Pause, Resume, Retry and Cancel.
steps.expect: With no file picked it says No files yet. If the network drops it says Connection lost. Trying again, attempt 1 of 3.
steps.why: Adding a late slide to an existing case must not need the whole upload page.

chapters.title: The viewer, its tabs and tools
chapters.intro: The viewer shows one whole slide like a map. Its top bar has Back, the slide name with the slide list, the mode switch Look, Review, Guided and Annotate, Export and Whole slide. The side panel has the tabs Objects, Display, Comments and Opinion, and I hides it. The left rail holds the tools. Press ? at any time for the shortcut sheet.

steps.title: Open a slide on its own
steps.click: Open the link. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom, press + and minus to zoom, 0 to fit, Z and hold to see the whole slide, and Alt with 1 to 6 for the objective.
steps.expect: The slide opens in Look mode within a few seconds, tiles sharpen as you zoom and the camera stops at the slide edge.
steps.why: Smooth viewing is the base of every other feature. Viv is the main renderer and must work perfectly.

steps.title: The Objects tab
steps.click: Open Objects in the side panel. Click a region such as T1 in the list, then press Shift F to zoom to it. Use G then a number, or the [ and ] keys, to jump between AI areas.
steps.expect: The list shows the AI result sets of the slide and their objects with short IDs such as T2 and T2·C145. Clicking one centres it.
steps.why: Short IDs let people talk about one object out loud and find it again.

steps.title: The Display tab
steps.click: Open Display. Change outline or fill, line width, opacity, colour by class, ID labels and the confidence cut-off. Press A to hide overlays, F to toggle fill and Shift with 1 to 4 for presets.
steps.expect: The overlay changes at once without reloading the slide.
steps.why: Reviewers read cells better with their own display, and a task can lock some choices so everyone sees the same thing.

steps.title: The Comments tab
steps.click: Open Comments. Press C, Comment on an ID, and click an object to start a thread on it.
steps.expect: Threads of this slide list with their object ID. A new thread pins to the object.
steps.why: Discussion stays attached to the exact cell or region it is about.

steps.title: Measure, whole slide and the minimap
steps.click: Press L for Measure and drag across tissue. Press Whole slide in the top bar. Hold Space to pan while another tool is on.
steps.expect: The ruler shows micrometres or millimetres from the slide's real pixel size. Whole slide fits the tissue.
steps.why: Pathologists measure deposits and margins, and the number must be right for each scanner.

steps.title: Compare slides
steps.click: Press Compare slides in the top bar, pick a second slide, and press Close compare when done. Q and E move to the previous and next slide.
steps.expect: Two slides side by side that pan and zoom together.
steps.why: Comparing levels or stains of one case is daily work for a pathologist.

steps.title: Export the objects of a slide
steps.click: Open Export in the top bar. Look at GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf, Parfocal JSON, Training dataset (QuPath GeoJSON zip), Patches with masks and Dataset page. Pick GeoJSON.
steps.expect: A file downloads with every object of the slide.
steps.why: Results leave the app in the formats QuPath and training code read.

steps.title: Every format opens
steps.click: Open this MIRAX slide, then use the slide list in the top bar to open CMU-1-JP2K-33005-v2 (DICOM), Leica-1.scn, OS-1.bif, Argos-1.avs and synthetic-zlib.ome.tiff.
steps.expect: Each one opens and its tiles look right, without a conversion step.
steps.why: Labs use many scanners. Reading each format natively avoids slow conversions.

steps.title: A slide whose file is missing
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: The viewer shows The slide file is not available instead of an empty canvas, with a way back.
steps.why: A broken file must explain itself, so nobody thinks the tissue is blank.

steps.title: A second window for the minimap
steps.click: Open the slide in one tab first, then this link in a new window on a second screen.
steps.expect: Opened alone it says Open this window from the viewer or Waiting for the main window. Next to an open viewer it says Following the main window and moves with it.
steps.why: Pathologists with two screens keep the overview or the inspector on the second one.

steps.title: Smart select, the one-click outline
steps.click: Press S for Smart select and click once on a cell or a gland. Keep the outline, fix it or throw it away.
steps.expect: An outline appears around what you clicked after a moment. The first call of the day can show Waiting for a GPU for a minute or two.
steps.why: Drawing cells by hand is slow. One click outlines make annotation many times faster.

steps.title: A viewer can look but not change
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and open the link. Try to draw with P.
steps.expect: The viewer says You can look at this slide but not change it. The drawing tools do nothing.
steps.why: Read-only people must never change data by accident.

steps.title: The old live viewer address
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: It moves on to the normal viewer of test_065 by itself.
steps.why: Links shared before the viewers were merged keep working.

chapters.title: Drawing and annotate tasks
chapters.intro: In an annotate task, experts improve one shared drawing together instead of judging the AI one by one. They draw with the pen, the brush or Smart select, confirm or delete AI objects, and mark each slide checked. The researcher then signs each slide off.

steps.title: Open the annotate task
steps.click: Sign in as role-annotator@parfocal.eu. Either press Continue on Home or open the link.
steps.expect: The first slide of Role account annotation opens in Annotate mode. The mode switch is fixed to Annotate.
steps.why: An expert should land straight on the drawing with nothing to set up.

steps.title: The drawing tools
steps.click: Try the rail one tool at a time: Polygon P, Freehand Shift P, Rectangle R, Ellipse O, Brush B, Count marker M, Ruler L, Arrow Shift L and Text T. Press 1 to 9 to give a shape a class, Enter to edit its points and Backspace to delete it.
steps.expect: Each shape appears on the shared layer with an ID such as T7 with a small plus, which says a person drew it.
steps.why: Experts draw the training truth themselves when the AI is wrong or missing.

steps.title: Smart select with Best
steps.click: Press S and click a cell. Switch the model to Best and click again.
steps.expect: An outline appears per click. Best is slower and sharper. A cold GPU shows Waiting for a GPU first.
steps.why: One click outlines make a training set affordable in expert time.

steps.title: Auto region
steps.click: Press U for Auto region and drag a box over a tumour area.
steps.expect: The app proposes a region outline inside the box, which you keep or discard.
steps.why: Large regions are tedious to trace by hand.

steps.title: The guided check of AI objects
steps.click: Press Shift G for Guided check. Use Confirm D, Skip Shift E, Delete Shift X and Next class Shift Y, then Leave the guided check. Restore the AI original undoes your edit of an AI object.
steps.expect: Each AI object gets a check state: unchecked, confirmed, edited or deleted. The counts update as you go.
steps.why: Every AI object a person checked is marked as such in the training data.

steps.title: Groups and select all
steps.click: Select some shapes, press Cmd G to group them and Shift Cmd G to ungroup. Cmd A selects all. Rename a group in the side panel.
steps.expect: Groups show in the panel with their count and can be renamed, filled or deleted.
steps.why: Experts organise many shapes, such as all lymph node deposits, in one place.

steps.title: Mark the slide checked
steps.click: Press Mark slide checked in the panel. On an empty slide the same place offers nothing to mark.
steps.expect: The slide shows as checked by you. The researcher sees it in the task's progress.
steps.why: A slide can be signed off only when every expert has checked it.

steps.title: A worked and signed off annotate slide
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu. Open the link and look through the layer panel.
steps.expect: Philips-3.tiff has shapes in classes and groups, AI cells confirmed, edited and deleted, a ruler and a note. Two experts checked it and it is signed off. The owner may still edit.
steps.why: This is the finished state an annotate task works towards.

steps.title: Blind first, every AI object checked, nothing to mark
steps.click: Open the task and move between its slides with the slide list.
steps.expect: The task uses blind first and requires every AI object to be checked. One slide has no results and both experts marked it nothing to mark. Both slides are signed off.
steps.why: These rules keep experts from copying each other and make sure nothing the AI made slips through unchecked.

steps.title: An empty slide to practise on
steps.click: Draw a tumour outline, confirm it and mark the slide checked.
steps.expect: The slide starts empty and keeps what you draw. A reseed clears it.
steps.why: A safe place to try every tool without touching the examples.

steps.title: The older annotate address
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: It moves on to the viewer in Annotate mode by itself.
steps.why: Older links to the annotate view keep working.

steps.title: The older annotate task address
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: It moves on to the viewer in Annotate mode by itself.
steps.why: Older links to the annotate task view keep working.

steps.title: Someone not on the task cannot draw
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: The viewer says You are not assigned to this task, so you can look but not change anything, or You can look at this slide but not change it.
steps.why: Only the experts of a task may change its shared drawing.

steps.title: An annotate task has no disagreement queue
steps.click: Open the link, then press Open the task.
steps.expect: Annotate tasks have no disagreements.
steps.why: Experts agree on one drawing, so there is nothing to compare.

chapters.title: Creating review tasks
chapters.intro: A review task hands slides and an AI result to two or more reviewers, who each judge every object on their own. The wizard has six short steps: Kind, Slides, Reviewers, What to check, How it runs and Send. Walk through it with Next and stop before the last button, unless you want a throwaway task that the next reseed removes.

steps.title: Kind, review or annotate
steps.click: From the project press New review task. Pick Review AI results and press Next.
steps.expect: The wizard opens on Kind with the steps listed across the top.
steps.why: Review and annotate tasks check work in different ways, so the choice comes first.

steps.title: Slides and the AI result
steps.click: Pick a few slides and the AI result set to check on each.
steps.expect: Each slide shows which result it has. A slide without results is marked.
steps.why: Reviewers judge one named AI result, so the evaluation knows exactly what it measured.

steps.title: Reviewers
steps.click: Pick Reviewer A and Reviewer B. Everyone reviews all gives agreement numbers. Look at each person's workload and availability.
steps.expect: The people of the workspace list with how busy they are.
steps.why: Two independent reviewers are what makes a disagreement measurable.

steps.title: What to check
steps.click: Pick the scope, such as all regions, random cells per slide, cells below a score or inside a drawn area. Then pick the decision style and read its Counts as line.
steps.expect: The decision styles are Agree with the AI, Yes or no, a certainty scale from Certainly not to Certainly, and a blind class pick. On the 5 point scale, 4 and 5 count as agree.
steps.why: The question decides what the evaluation can say about the AI.

steps.title: How it runs
steps.click: Choose blind or not, guided review or the full viewer, a due date and reminders, and the display defaults reviewers start with.
steps.expect: Blind is on by default, which hides each reviewer's answers from the other.
steps.why: Blind review keeps reviewers from copying each other, and a due date drives the reminders.

steps.title: Send, and what blocks it
steps.click: Read the summary with a Change link back to each step. If something is missing, a box Before you can send lists it with a Go to link. Create and notify 2 reviewers would send it.
steps.expect: Every choice is listed in one place. After sending: Back to the project and Track it in Team.
steps.why: One last look before people are notified avoids tasks that have to be withdrawn.

steps.title: The annotate task wizard
steps.click: Pick Annotate. The presets are Annotate by hand, Check a whole slide run, a sample, regions and mixed. Walk the steps Kind, Slides, Experts, What to check, How it runs and Send.
steps.expect: The blockers are Name the task, Pick at least one slide and Pick at least one expert. Send to experts would create it, then Open the task.
steps.why: Annotate tasks make training data from scratch or from the AI's shapes.

steps.title: What I handed out
steps.click: Open My work, then Assigned by me. Use Nudge, Change due date, Add reviewer, Reassign slides and Preview on a task row.
steps.expect: Every task the researcher sent, with how far each reviewer is. A researcher who sent nothing sees You have not handed out any review tasks yet.
steps.why: The researcher follows their tasks without opening each one.

chapters.title: Reviewing, as each reviewer
chapters.intro: Each reviewer judges every object of their slides alone. Guided review shows one object at a time, and the full viewer in Review mode saves to the same review. A decision counts as agree, not sure or disagree. A reviewer can also fix an object by redrawing, retyping or adding what the AI missed. Role account review has two reviewers, A and B, on two slides of the format gallery.

steps.title: My work, To review
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-a@parfocal.eu. Open My work. The tabs are To review, Assigned by me and All slides. Press Start in guided review on Role account review.
steps.expect: Role account review shows with 0 of 2 slides and a Start in guided review button.
steps.why: A reviewer finds all their work in one list.

steps.title: Guided review opens the first object
steps.click: Open the link, or press Start in guided review.
steps.expect: The first slide opens in Guided mode with one object centred and outlined and its decision buttons in the panel.
steps.why: One object at a time is the fastest way to judge hundreds of objects without missing one.

steps.title: Agree, disagree, not sure
steps.click: Press Agree or K on the first object. On the next press Disagree or X, then pick What is wrong and Quick reasons, optional. Press Not sure or U on a third. J is Skip for now, Shift J is Previous, Shift K is Agree with the rest and Shift N is Add a note.
steps.expect: Each press saves at once and moves to the next object. The dots show which objects are decided.
steps.why: These answers are the data the evaluation is built from.

steps.title: Fix an object
steps.click: On the object card press Change the type and pick another class. On another press Redraw the outline or Edit shape. Press Add something the AI missed and draw it.
steps.expect: The fix shows on the slide and is kept in a history that is never erased. The AI's own object stays untouched.
steps.why: A reviewer's fix becomes the outline or class in the training data when the queue agrees.

steps.title: The full viewer saves to the same review
steps.click: Switch the mode from Guided to Review. Click any object on the slide and decide it in the panel. P is Annotate this slide and Shift A opens AI tools.
steps.expect: The decisions made in guided review show here too, and new ones show there.
steps.why: Some reviewers prefer to scan the whole slide. Both ways must give one review.

steps.title: The opinion form
steps.click: Open the Opinion tab and answer the questions.
steps.expect: The slide's questions show, or No opinion asked if the task has none. Required questions block the submit until answered.
steps.why: Some answers are about the whole slide, such as how acceptable the AI result is.

steps.title: Submit the slide
steps.click: When every object is decided, press Submit the slide or Enter. The submitted page counts down.
steps.expect: Slide 1 submitted. Opens by itself in a few seconds, with Open slide 2 and Back to My work. The review can still change until the researcher signs off.
steps.why: Submitting tells the researcher this reviewer is done with the slide.

steps.title: Reviewer B works alone
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-b@parfocal.eu in a second private window and review the same slide.
steps.expect: Reviewer B sees none of Reviewer A's answers, only the AI's objects.
steps.why: Blind review is what makes the agreement between reviewers mean something.

steps.title: All slides
steps.click: Open My work, All slides. Filter by project and status, then Clear filters.
steps.expect: Every slide the reviewer can see, with its state. A filter with no match says No slide matches these filters.
steps.why: A reviewer can find any slide again, not only the next one.

steps.title: Cells judged on the slide
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu. Open the link. Move between the twelve random cells with the small cells panel and decide each.
steps.expect: The viewer opens in cells mode with the current cell centred and outlined.
steps.why: Random cells give an unbiased estimate of how well the AI types cells.

steps.title: Four ways to ask
steps.click: Open each of Agree decisions review, Certainty decisions review, Yes-no decisions review and Blind decisions review from the project's Review tasks tab, and look at the buttons.
steps.expect: Agree K, Disagree X and Not sure U. Certainly not to Certainly on 1 to 5. Yes Y, No N and Not sure U. Blind shows class names on 1 to 4 without the AI's guess.
steps.why: The style is chosen per task, and each one is turned into agree, not sure or disagree by its Counts as line.

steps.title: Someone not on the task can only look
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: You are not assigned to this task, so you can look but not change anything. No decision buttons work.
steps.why: Only the assigned reviewers may add answers.

steps.title: A signed off task is locked
steps.click: Open the link and try to change a decision.
steps.expect: The task is signed off. An owner can reopen it.
steps.why: After sign-off the answers are final and the report stays true.

steps.title: The task address alone
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: It moves on to guided review of your next open slide by itself.
steps.why: Links to a task always lead to the work that is left.

chapters.title: The disagreement queue and adjudication
chapters.intro: When every reviewer has submitted, the app compares their answers. An object goes to the queue when reviewers differ, when both say the AI is wrong, when someone asked for a second look, or when their redrawn outlines overlap less than the task's threshold of 60 percent. The researcher decides it, leaves it open on purpose, asks both to look again, or sends it to an adjudicator, who sees the reviewers only as Reviewer A and Reviewer B.

steps.title: Open the queue
steps.click: Sign in as role-researcher@parfocal.eu. From the study project's Review tasks tab press Disagreements on Disagreement queue example, or open the link.
steps.expect: Disagreements in Disagreement queue example. Each row shows the AI and both reviewers side by side, the reason it is here, and the buttons.
steps.why: This is where the final answer of every contested object is made.

steps.title: Decide a row
steps.click: On an open row press Decide with the task's own buttons, or Keep as a class, or Keep with the reviewer's type, or Redraw it myself.
steps.expect: The row moves to decided and the count of open rows drops.
steps.why: Agree keeps the object, disagree leaves it out, and a chosen class or outline is what goes into the training data.

steps.title: Leave a row open, or ask to look again
steps.click: On another row press Leave open and write why. On a third press Ask both to look again.
steps.expect: A left open row is counted and named in the report. A look again row goes back to both reviewers with your note, and their old answers stay in the history.
steps.why: Some objects cannot be decided from this slide, and the report must say so honestly.

steps.title: Send to an adjudicator
steps.click: Tick a row and press Send to an adjudicator. Pick a person who was not a reviewer and send.
steps.expect: The row shows as with the adjudicator. Send to someone else changes the person.
steps.why: A neutral referee settles what the researcher should not decide alone.

steps.title: A finished queue with every outcome
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu and open the link. Read the reasons and answers of each row.
steps.expect: Every reason shows: reviewers differ, both against the AI, second look and outlines differ. The answers are agree, disagree, keep the reviewer's type, use Rhea's outline, an adjudicator's answer, a look again and one left open on purpose.
steps.why: This is the reference of what every queue answer does.

steps.title: Disagree and choose a class
steps.click: Open the link and find the row decided by naming a class.
steps.expect: The object stays in the data with the class the researcher chose.
steps.why: An AI object with the wrong class is still useful once its class is fixed.

steps.title: Drawn objects in the queue
steps.click: Open the link. One object was drawn by hand and one with Smart select.
steps.expect: Drawn objects carry IDs with a small plus, such as T7 plus, and read as drawn, not as AI.
steps.why: A review task can check a colleague's drawing, not only the AI.

steps.title: The queue before everyone submitted
steps.click: Open the link while Reviewer A or B still has slides left.
steps.expect: Nothing to decide yet. The queue opens when every reviewer has submitted, with Nudge for the reviewer who is behind.
steps.why: Comparing half finished reviews would be unfair to the slower reviewer.

steps.title: The adjudicator's My work
steps.click: Sign in as role-adjudicator@parfocal.eu. Open My work.
steps.expect: One object sent to you, with Start deciding.
steps.why: The adjudicator only sees what was sent to them.

steps.title: Decide as the adjudicator
steps.click: Press Start deciding, or open the link. Read the card that says who asked you to decide. Decide the object with the task's buttons. Previous, Next and Skip for now move between objects, and Open in Review shows the full viewer.
steps.expect: The reviewers show as Reviewer A and Reviewer B, never by name. Your answer goes back to the researcher's queue.
steps.why: An anonymous referee judges the work, not the person.

steps.title: Nothing to adjudicate
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-a@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: Nothing is queued for you on this task. Back to My work.
steps.why: Only the person a row was sent to can decide it.

chapters.title: Sign off, evaluation, dataset and exports
chapters.intro: Sign off makes a review task final. It needs every slide submitted, every queue row decided or left open on purpose, and a sign-in from the last five minutes. At sign off the app builds the final layer, the clean checked answer per slide, and the evaluation report. The Dataset page turns the final layer into training files and frozen versions.

steps.title: What blocks a sign off
steps.click: Open the link. Each blocker has a link, such as See them in the disagreements or Back to disagreements.
steps.expect: Before you can sign, with the open queue rows and anyone with slides left, such as Rhea has 1 slide left.
steps.why: A task cannot be signed while answers are missing, so the report is never built on half the data.

steps.title: A signed task
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu and open the link. Press Download 3 files.
steps.expect: Evaluation v1 is signed. The counts, the signature with its checksum, the change after sign off and the three files: report PDF, decisions CSV and evaluation JSON.
steps.why: The signature and checksum prove the files were not changed after signing.

steps.title: Sign a task yourself
steps.click: First decide every open row of Disagreement queue example in its queue. Then press Sign off Disagreement queue example and Sign v1. If your sign-in is older than five minutes, enter your password again.
steps.expect: Ready to sign, then Evaluation v1 is signed. Reviewers are told. Open the evaluation report and Start v2 appear.
steps.why: A fresh sign-in means nobody can sign at a laptop left open.

steps.title: The evaluation report
steps.click: Open Evaluation from the task row. Press Preview the PDF, then Download or Download CSV only. Arrange blocks and format changes the layout.
steps.expect: The report pages show agreement with the AI per class, errors by reason and every object by ID, laid out by the study template.
steps.why: This is what goes into a paper or to a supervisor.

steps.title: Changes after sign off
steps.click: Scroll to the change table, or Switch to another version.
steps.expect: One change after sign off, with the reason A pathologist meeting found tumour on the deeper level. The signed checksum still belongs to the version as signed.
steps.why: The owner can still correct data after signing, and every change leaves a trace.

steps.title: Share the report by link
steps.click: Press Compare and share, then Make a link, Copy, and later Revoke.
steps.expect: A read-only link that anyone can open without an account until you revoke it.
steps.why: Co-authors read the report without joining the workspace.

steps.title: A shared link that does not work
steps.click: Open the link in a private window.
steps.expect: This link does not lead to a report. A revoked link says This link was revoked or has expired.
steps.why: A stranger with a dead link learns nothing about the study.

steps.title: The final layer
steps.click: Open the Dataset page. Filter By origin and By class. Tick Include AI objects nobody checked to see the difference. Build the final layer again rebuilds it after a change.
steps.expect: Counts per slide of ai-confirmed, ai-edited, rejected and human objects, and the one left open on purpose.
steps.why: Only what a person checked goes into training data, and what was left out is counted.

steps.title: Frozen dataset versions
steps.click: Under versions, press Download on version 1, First frozen training set. Freeze a version would make version 2.
steps.expect: A zip with one QuPath GeoJSON per slide and a manifest with a SHA-256 per file.
steps.why: A frozen version never changes, so an experiment can be repeated months later.

steps.title: Patches with masks and COCO
steps.click: Under Patch exports, download the COCO export of version 1. Cut patches would start a new export as a job.
steps.expect: A zip of tiles, masks and a COCO file. A new export runs as a job and sends a notice when done.
steps.why: Pixel models train on patches and masks, many tools read COCO.

steps.title: The training dataset of a signed task
steps.click: Open the link and press Download.
steps.expect: A zip of the signed slides.
steps.why: Every signed review task can feed training directly.

steps.title: No dataset before sign off
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Sign off the review task first. Its final layer is built from the signed off decisions.
steps.why: Training on unfinished answers would put unchecked data into a model.

steps.title: An annotate task's dataset
steps.click: Open the link and download.
steps.expect: The signed off annotate slide with its drawn and checked objects. Arrows, text notes and rulers are only counted, never exported.
steps.why: Annotate tasks feed the same training files as review tasks.

steps.title: An annotate task has no evaluation
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Annotate tasks have no evaluation, with a way back to the task.
steps.why: There is no AI answer being measured in an annotate task.

chapters.title: Cases and clinical reports
chapters.intro: Only a clinical project has cases. A case holds one patient's slides and ends in a clinical report written in steps: findings, staging, report text and sign. A member with the right to sign out signs it. Anyone else sends it for co-sign. The seed has three cases in Breast surgery sentinel nodes: Showcase case, Showcase draft report and Showcase co-sign.

steps.title: The clinical project and its cases
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu. Open the clinical project. Slides are grouped by case, and a case row has Open report.
steps.expect: The three cases and the loose slide Missing file.svs.
steps.why: Clinical work is organised by patient, not by slide.

steps.title: Review a case in the viewer
steps.click: Open the link. The top bar has Open report next to Submit. Cmd Enter signs out the case.
steps.expect: The case slides open in the same viewer, and the report is one click away.
steps.why: The pathologist moves from the slide to the report without losing their place.

steps.title: A case address opens its report
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: It moves on to the report of Showcase case by itself.
steps.why: The report is what a case is for.

steps.title: Findings
steps.click: Open the draft report. If it has none yet, press Start the report. Read the findings, which come from the decisions on the slides, and press Next.
steps.expect: The findings list with the objects they come from.
steps.why: The report text starts from what was seen on the slide, not from a blank page.

steps.title: Staging with several deposits
steps.click: Look at the deposit rows. Add one measured by hand. Pick the category and extranodal extension. Press Next.
steps.expect: The largest deposit sets the suggested category, which stays a suggestion until you pick it. The suggested pN follows.
steps.why: Staging decides treatment, so the app suggests and the doctor decides.

steps.title: The report text
steps.click: Edit the text. Use the chips that insert measurements from the slide. Press Next.
steps.expect: The text is filled in from the findings and staging.
steps.why: Pre-filled text saves time and keeps numbers right.

steps.title: Sign out, or send for co-sign
steps.click: With the right to sign out, the step offers Sign out and Send for co-sign instead. Without it, Send for co-sign, and after sending Withdraw the request.
steps.expect: Signed out: the case is signed out and goes to the clinician, with Download PDF and Amend. Sent: Sent to a name, waiting.
steps.why: Only a doctor with the right may release a report. Others must pass it to one.

steps.title: Co-sign a colleague's report
steps.click: Open My work, or the link. Compare the sender's values with yours and the AI's. Press Co-sign and sign out, or Return with a note.
steps.expect: Changed rows highlight. After signing: Co-signed and signed out. The report names you both.
steps.why: A trainee's report is checked and signed by a senior, and both names stay on it.

steps.title: Only the asked person can co-sign
steps.click: Sign in as role-researcher@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: Only the named person can co-sign this report. Nothing can be signed here.
steps.why: A co-sign request belongs to one person.

steps.title: A case without a co-sign request
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Nobody has sent this report for co-sign yet.
steps.why: The co-sign page explains itself instead of showing an empty form.

chapters.title: Jobs and model runs
chapters.intro: Uploads, model runs and patch exports run as jobs. The jobs button in the top bar shows how many run, and each job has a progress window you can close while it keeps going. Model runs use a GPU in the EU on demand. They cost money and the first one after a quiet spell waits for a cold start, which the app shows as Waiting for a GPU.

steps.title: The jobs tray
steps.click: Press the jobs button in the top bar, which reads the number of jobs running.
steps.expect: Running and recent jobs with their progress, each opening its own window.
steps.why: Long work never blocks the page you are on.

steps.title: One job's progress window
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu and open the link to the seeded upload job. The buttons are Close, it keeps going, Open the slide and Open the project. A running model run adds Cancel the run, Resume now and Move it to another GPU.
steps.expect: The upload of Philips-4.tiff shows as done at 100 percent.
steps.why: Anyone can see what a job did and jump to its result.

steps.title: Run a model, pick
steps.click: From the project's More menu press Run a model. Pick a Model, add slides under Slides with Add slides by name or case, and read the time estimate. Connect your own model leads to the lab model setup.
steps.expect: With no slide picked it says No slides picked yet. With slides the button reads Run on 2 slides.
steps.why: A researcher fills in slides that came without results.

steps.title: Run a model, start
steps.click: Press Run on 1 slide with one small slide such as CMU-1-Small-Region.svs. Then watch the progress window and close it.
steps.expect: The job starts, shows Waiting for a GPU if the pool is cold, then counts tiles and ends with a new result set on the slide.
steps.why: This is the real AI inference the whole review is about. It costs GPU seconds.

steps.title: Find nuclei on part of a slide
steps.click: Press Shift A for AI tools and pick Find nuclei on the area in view.
steps.expect: The panel shows the run's progress and the new cells appear on the slide.
steps.why: An expert gets AI cells on just the part they are working on.

steps.title: Task timing
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Task timing figures, or No timing recorded yet. Figures appear as people who allow analytics finish tasks.
steps.why: The thesis measures how long review takes. This page shows those numbers.

chapters.title: Search
chapters.intro: Search finds projects, cases, slides, object IDs such as T2·C145, people and actions. It works from the top bar, from Cmd K anywhere, and as its own page with scope chips.

steps.title: Search from the top bar
steps.click: Click the search box Search projects, slides, IDs like T2·C145, or press Cmd K, and type CMU.
steps.expect: The command palette lists matching slides with their project. Enter opens the first.
steps.why: With hundreds of slides, typing a name is faster than browsing.

steps.title: The search page and its scopes
steps.click: Press the scope chips All, Projects, Cases, Slides, Object IDs, People and Actions.
steps.expect: The results narrow to each kind. Every hit opens its page.
steps.why: The same word can mean a slide, a case or a person.

steps.title: Search for an object ID
steps.click: Open the link and pick a hit.
steps.expect: The slide opens with that object centred.
steps.why: A colleague can say T2 on Case queue 1 and anyone finds it.

steps.title: Too short to search
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Type at least two letters to search.
steps.why: One letter would match everything.

steps.title: Nothing matches
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Nothing matches zzqqxx.
steps.why: An empty result says so in words.

steps.title: Search as a viewer
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and search for Case.
steps.expect: Only what the viewer may see appears.
steps.why: Search must never leak a project someone is not in.

chapters.title: Notifications and comments
chapters.intro: The bell counts unread notifications, such as a task sent to you, an object to adjudicate, a nudge or a mention. Each one opens exactly what it points at. Comments are threads pinned to an object ID, and anyone in the task can mention a colleague.

steps.title: The bell and the notifications page
steps.click: Sign in as role-adjudicator@parfocal.eu. Press the bell in the top bar, then open the full list. Press Mark all read and Show older.
steps.expect: A notice that an object was sent to you to decide. With nothing new the page says Nothing here yet.
steps.why: People learn about new work without email.

steps.title: A notification opens its target
steps.click: Click the notification.
steps.expect: Opening the notification, then the adjudication page or task it points at.
steps.why: One click from the notice to the work.

steps.title: A notification whose target is gone
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: This notification cannot be opened. What it points at was deleted, or it is no longer open to you. A button leads to the notifications.
steps.why: Old notices must fail politely.

steps.title: A task's comment threads
steps.click: Open Comments of Every outcome review. Read the thread Is this the same tumour as the next region. Close the thread resolves it, and Your decision notes lists your own notes.
steps.expect: The thread is pinned to its object, with an @mention of a colleague.
steps.why: Questions about a single object stay with that object.

steps.title: Start a thread and mention someone
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-a@parfocal.eu. Press C, Comment on an ID, click an object, write a question and type @ to mention the researcher.
steps.expect: The thread appears in Comments and the mentioned person gets a notification.
steps.why: Reviewers ask the researcher instead of guessing.

steps.title: A case thread you can reply to
steps.click: Open the case slide's Comments and reply to the thread.
steps.expect: Your reply shows under the thread at once.
steps.why: Clinical colleagues discuss a case slide in place.

steps.title: Nudge a reviewer
steps.click: On Team press Nudge next to a reviewer who is behind, or Nudge all behind.
steps.expect: The reviewer gets a notification that says how far they are and when the task is due. With nobody behind: Nobody is behind right now.
steps.why: A researcher keeps a study on time without writing emails.

steps.title: Choose what you are told about
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-b@parfocal.eu. Open the avatar menu, Settings, then Notifications. Switch a kind of notice off and on.
steps.expect: Each kind of notice can be turned on or off for the app and for email.
steps.why: People decide how much they are interrupted.

chapters.title: Team, settings and admin
chapters.intro: Team shows who reviews what. Settings are personal and open as an overlay from the avatar menu or Cmd comma. Admin is the workspace's control room and only opens for a researcher with admin rights, which here is only agent-walk. The developer drawer is for researchers.

steps.title: Team, open tasks
steps.click: Open Team in the sidebar. Filter by project, reviewer or task. Reassign slides from a reviewer who is away.
steps.expect: Every open task with each reviewer's progress and who is behind.
steps.why: The researcher spots a stuck study before its due date.

steps.title: Team, done
steps.click: Open the Done tab.
steps.expect: Signed off tasks, or No signed-off task matches these filters.
steps.why: A record of finished work per person.

steps.title: Settings open on Display
steps.click: Open the avatar menu and Settings, or press Cmd comma. Type in the filter at the top to find a setting.
steps.expect: It opens on Display. The sections are Display, Review, Layout, AI and confidence, Navigation and devices, Shortcuts, Notifications, Privacy and session and Account.
steps.why: Each person tunes the viewer to their eyes and hands.

steps.title: Review and Layout settings
steps.click: Look at Review, then Layout at /settings/layout. Change how the next object is chosen and where the panel sits.
steps.expect: Each change applies at once and shows where a task locks it.
steps.why: Reviewers work faster with the order and layout they like, within what the task allows.

steps.title: AI and confidence
steps.click: Change how confidence shows, as a number or a bar.
steps.expect: The viewer follows the setting.
steps.why: Some reviewers want to see the AI's certainty, some want to avoid its pull.

steps.title: Navigation, devices and shortcuts
steps.click: Pick a device such as Mouse, Trackpad, Gamepad, Tablet and pen or Keyboard. Then open Shortcuts at /settings/shortcuts and change one key. A key already in use shows a conflict.
steps.expect: The viewer's controls follow the device, and the shortcut sheet shows your keys.
steps.why: Pathologists come from QuPath or other viewers and keep their habits.

steps.title: Privacy, session and account
steps.click: Look at Privacy and session, with Sign out on other devices and Add a passkey. Then Account at /settings/account, and Show all hints again.
steps.expect: Your sessions and passkeys list, each with Remove.
steps.why: People control where they are signed in and how.

steps.title: An unknown settings section
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found.
steps.why: A wrong link fails clearly.

steps.title: The avatar menu
steps.click: Open the avatar menu. Try Keyboard shortcuts, Profile and signature, Send feedback, Help and what's new, Lock the screen and Log out.
steps.expect: Lock the screen hides the app until you sign in again. Send feedback opens a short form.
steps.why: A pathologist leaving the desk locks the screen in one click.

steps.title: Admin overview
steps.click: Sign in as agent-walk@parfocal.eu and open Admin in the sidebar. The side nav has Back to Parfocal, Overview, People and roles, Projects, AI models, Report templates, Storage and sources, API and webhooks, Audit log, Security and Workspace settings.
steps.expect: The overview shows members, projects, storage and AI use of the workspace.
steps.why: One place to run the workspace.

steps.title: People and roles
steps.click: Look at the members and their roles. Invite opens the invite window. Do not change the role accounts.
steps.expect: Every member with role and project roles, and pending access requests.
steps.why: Admins decide who may see and change what.

steps.title: Projects in admin
steps.click: Look at the list, including deleted projects that can be restored.
steps.expect: Every project with its owner and size.
steps.why: Admins clean up and restore projects.

steps.title: AI models and their use
steps.click: Look at the models, which ones are hidden, the model tiers and the AI use with GPU seconds.
steps.expect: Each model with its version and the GPU seconds the workspace used.
steps.why: GPU time costs money, so admins see and limit it.

steps.title: Report templates
steps.click: Open a study template and its preview.
steps.expect: The templates with their versions and a preview of the report they make.
steps.why: The template decides how every evaluation report is laid out.

steps.title: Storage and sources
steps.click: Look at storage use and the import sources.
steps.expect: Bytes used per project and the connected storage.
steps.why: Slides are big. Admins watch the bill.

steps.title: API and webhooks
steps.click: Look at the webhooks and the API settings.
steps.expect: The webhook list, empty or with targets.
steps.why: A lab's own systems hear about finished tasks.

steps.title: Audit log
steps.click: Filter the log by person or action and export it.
steps.expect: Every sign-in, sign off and change with who and when.
steps.why: Every action on medical data must be traceable.

steps.title: Security and workspace settings
steps.click: Look at Security, then Workspace settings at /admin?section=settings.
steps.expect: The session policy, sign-in rules, retention and who may join.
steps.why: Each workspace sets its own security rules.

steps.title: Admin refused without admin rights
steps.click: Sign in as role-researcher@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: You do not have admin rights in this workspace.
steps.why: A researcher runs studies, not the workspace.

steps.title: Admin refused for a reviewer
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-b@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: The admin page is for people with admin rights.
steps.why: Reviewers never reach workspace settings.

steps.title: The developer drawer
steps.click: Open the sections Renderer, Tiles and source, Annotations, Heatmap, Models, Typing and confidence, Whole-slide job, Benchmark, HUD and URL and debug handle.
steps.expect: Each section shows its switches and numbers.
steps.why: Researchers tune and measure the viewer and models for the thesis.

steps.title: The developer drawer is refused
steps.click: Sign in as role-viewer@parfocal.eu and open the link.
steps.expect: Developer mode is not available. The developer drawer is for researchers. Reviewers and doctors review slides without it. Go home.
steps.why: Clinical users never see debug switches.

chapters.title: The study
chapters.intro: Study mode runs usability sessions for the thesis. A facilitator starts a session, gives a participant tasks one at a time, times them and downloads the results. Everything is kept in this browser only.

steps.title: Open study mode
steps.click: Open the link. Read the session list and press Run a session.
steps.expect: The study page with its tasks and past rounds.
steps.why: Measured sessions are the evidence that the app is fast and clear to use.

steps.title: Run a session
steps.click: Press Start session, then Start task for the first task. Mark it done, or use Skip or Gave up.
steps.expect: Each task is timed from Start task to its end.
steps.why: The times are compared across rounds.

steps.title: Edit the tasks and start the next round
steps.click: Change the task list and press Save tasks, then Start next round.
steps.expect: The new round uses the saved tasks.
steps.why: Each round tests the app after the fixes from the last one.

steps.title: Download and replay
steps.click: Press Download results. Press Replay on a past session, then Play and Pause.
steps.expect: A results file downloads. The replay shows what the participant did, step by step.
steps.why: The results go into the thesis, and the replay shows where people got stuck.

steps.title: A reviewer as participant
steps.click: Sign in as role-reviewer-a@parfocal.eu in the participant's browser and run one task.
steps.expect: The same page works for a reviewer, with their own slides.
steps.why: Participants in the study are reviewers, not researchers.

chapters.title: Pages only a development build shows
chapters.intro: These pages exist for designers and developers. The deployed app hides them unless public dev tools are switched on, so on app.parfocal.eu each of them should say Page not found. If one of them opens instead, dev tools are on.

steps.title: The error page gallery
steps.click: Open the link. In a dev build the kinds are not-found, server-error, expired, no-access and styles.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app. In a dev build, the shared error page of that kind.
steps.why: Every error page of the app can be checked in one place during design.

steps.title: Every error state by screen
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app. In a dev build, a list of every error state by screen.
steps.why: Designers check that every screen handles its failures.

steps.title: The flow map
steps.click: Open the link. In a dev build it shows one lane per person, with Walkthrough and Prototype index.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app.
steps.why: The map is the index of the core flow for the design work.

steps.title: The guided walkthrough
steps.click: Open the link. In a dev build: Walkthrough, nine chapters, and Play all, from upload to the signed report.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app.
steps.why: The mock walkthrough tells the story this page checks for real.

steps.title: One walkthrough chapter
steps.click: Open the link. In a dev build it plays chapter 1, Upload, with Back to the map.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app.
steps.why: Each chapter can be shown on its own in a meeting.

steps.title: The prototype index
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app. In a dev build, links to every mock scene.
steps.why: Designers jump to any mock state.

steps.title: The hotkeys spike
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app.
steps.why: A test bench for keyboard handling.

steps.title: The input traces spike
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app.
steps.why: A test bench that records pointer input for camera tests.

steps.title: The worklist spike
steps.click: Open the link.
steps.expect: Page not found on the deployed app. In a dev build, a list of 5000 rows that scrolls smoothly.
steps.why: A test bench for long lists.
